name: Pathwise Horizon-Consistent Residual Projection
parent_evidence: clean generator therefore requires deterministic rollout-state rather than latent-state calibration
unsb_object: pathwise squared remaining endpoint displacement over the nonuniform physical bridge horizon
mathematical_update: At bridge point i let P_i=G_theta(X_i,z_i), e_i=mean((P_i-X_i)^2), h_i=1-t_i. Set q_0=e_0 and for i>0 c_i=q_{i-1}h_i/h_{i-1}, a_i=min(1,sqrt(c_i/e_i)), Y_i=X_i+a_i(P_i-X_i), q_i=e_i*a_i^2. The same trajectory recursion is used in training rollout, the differentiable final endpoint and inference.
derivation: For a restricted Brownian bridge, the expected squared remaining displacement has first-order physical scaling O(h).
The admissible pathwise cone q_i<=q_{i-1}h_i/h_{i-1} enforces no-slower-than-linear decay without fixing HNEK's exponent gamma.
a_i is the Euclidean projection of the native residual onto the current cone ball; it is determined by the current trajectory and physical grid, not optimizer time.
If the native endpoint residual already decays at least linearly, a_i=1 and the implementation returns the native endpoint byte-for-byte.
When the raw residual energy follows h^beta, the induced local scale is exactly the missing physical exponent: a_i^2=(h_i/h_{i-1})^(1-beta) when beta<1.
The first bridge point is exact plain, so the algorithm introduces no external reference endpoint and no plain-output anchor.
long_horizon_property: the coordinate is recomputed on every actual bridge trajectory and self-nulls at every point where native physical scaling is sufficient
identity_condition: e_i<=q_{i-1}h_i/h_{i-1}, with the entire first bridge point always identity
self_null_condition: the current native remaining-displacement energy decays at least as fast as the physical remaining horizon
unbiased_or_invariance_property: native endpoints inside the pathwise physical cone and every t=0 endpoint are exact fixed points
paired_target_proof: the recursion reads only current rollout states, native endpoints and the fixed physical time grid
expected_valid_states: deterministic clean-UNSB trajectories whose endpoint residual sometimes decays more slowly than the remaining physical horizon
falsification_test: kill if pathwise cap, first-point identity, native-cone self-null, train/inference equivalence, zero-intervention or full-state resume fails; permit one causal revision only if a 400/800/1200 trajectory lowers the physical defect but remains late-negative
compute_cost: one native generator call plus scalar residual projection; no extra generator forward
memory_cost: three per-forward trajectory histories during training and one during inference; no persistent learned state
allowed_claim: tests whether fixed HNEK can be replaced by a trajectory-native self-null physical coordinate on the deterministic clean base
forbidden_claims: all deterministic endpoint contractions are safe
